# Delivery plan

This is the versioned scope and acceptance baseline for **Pick Your AI — AI Papers & Research Index**. The [GitHub receipt](../planning/github-receipt.json) records actual remote setup state. Prepared files do not establish a remote repository, Project, hosted CI, scientific catalog or live search service.

[Complete work packages](BACKLOG.md) · [Structured backlog](../planning/project-backlog.json) · [Coverage matrix](../planning/coverage-matrix.json) · [Decisions](../planning/decision-register.json) · [Release gates](../planning/release-manifest.json) · [Project setup](PROJECT_SETUP.md)

## Scope and hierarchy

The baseline defines **165 native issue outcomes**: one program, 20 epics and 144 independently reviewable work packages. The packages contain 432 tasks and 864 nested subtasks. The internal hierarchy has 164 planned parent edges and 270 genuine prerequisite edges. These are planned counts, not created-resource counts.

The parent [research audit #509](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/issues/509) is the program context. A separately verified cross-repository parent edge, if applied, is additional to the internal hierarchy count.

Program -> native epic issues -> native independently reviewable work-package issues -> nested checklist tasks/subtasks. A task becomes a native issue only after a separately reviewed ownership/acceptance boundary is needed.

GitHub Assignees are authoritative; initial work is unassigned. Versioned scope must not reset live status, ownership or accepted progress.

The user-supplied list ends midway through `02.05`. `PAPER-DEC-001` records the completion of that item and the inferred remaining scope. All eight supplied Epic 01 titles and the first four supplied Epic 02 titles are preserved.

## Status and qualification

All initial scope is **Backlog**, **unassigned** and **Not Accepted**. Role descriptions identify needed expertise; they do not appoint anyone. Publication Status is **Not Applicable** for planning aggregates. A paper’s peer-review/publication state, claim confidence, citation verification, source rights and reproduction evidence must be assessed in their own records. No relationship or status label supplies missing scientific evidence.

The backlog is a scope baseline, not a controller for live status. Do not overwrite accepted progress or native Assignees when reconciling issues. A documentation slice does not complete a package that also requires future research or implementation.

## Coverage and completeness

The matrix contains 102 declared subjects across 7 dimensions and maps every one of the 144 work packages. The dimensions include scientific domains, publication types, research objects, source families, research methods and failure states. Workstream denominators are known planning counts; real literature denominators remain unmeasured and the global denominator is unknown.

Near-exhaustive is a research objective. Coverage is measured only against explicit dated source/domain cohorts, never an assumed global universe.

Coverage reports must distinguish discovered candidates, screened records, exclusions, duplicate manifestations, reviewed fields and admitted public projections. An absent source, inaccessible work or unresolved identity stays visible as a gap. A sampled source union is not a census of all AI literature.

## Decisions and release sequence

The register contains 16 explicit decisions. It records owner roles and remaining gates without inventing an accepting person, source permission or organizational appointment.

### Foundation

**Exit criteria**

- Exact source revision passes offline validation and meaningful negative tests.
- Actual repository, Project fields/views/items and native graph have complete verified readback; any missing remote setup requirement keeps this phase unaccepted.
- Independent source review and organizational approval boundaries remain accurately recorded.

**Required packages:** `PAPER-19.01`, `PAPER-19.02`, `PAPER-19.03`, `PAPER-19.05`, `PAPER-19.06`, `PAPER-20.01`.

**Not established by this phase alone:** An operating search engine; A verified scientific catalog; Completion of future research outcomes.

### Metadata Pilot

**Exit criteria**

- A bounded real candidate cohort has a dated denominator and exclusion log.
- Every admitted field has exact-version source, rights and editorial evidence.
- Unknowns, conflicts, inaccessible sources and rejected records remain visible.

**Required packages:** `PAPER-02.10`, `PAPER-03.06`, `PAPER-13.04`, `PAPER-18.01`, `PAPER-20.02`.

**Not established by this phase alone:** Global literature completeness; Scientific correctness of indexed claims.

### Evidence Pilot

**Exit criteria**

- Claim summaries preserve study context and contradictory evidence.
- Any reproduction label resolves to actual independent execution receipts.
- Corrections and graph provenance are verified for the selected pilot.

**Required packages:** `PAPER-08.06`, `PAPER-10.07`, `PAPER-11.03`, `PAPER-16.03`, `PAPER-20.03`.

**Not established by this phase alone:** Universal reproducibility; A consensus ranking of methods.

### Website Handoff

**Exit criteria**

- Exact admitted snapshot and consumer revision pass actual receiving tests.
- Source, rights, uncertainty and correction states remain visible in public journeys.
- Website owner accepts publication and records actual deployment/readback separately.

**Required packages:** `PAPER-15.07`, `PAPER-17.02`, `PAPER-17.03`, `PAPER-17.05`, `PAPER-17.06`, `PAPER-17.07`, `PAPER-20.04`.

**Not established by this phase alone:** Deployment from local fixtures alone; Unaccepted mobile integration.

### Maintained Index

**Exit criteria**

- Actual stewardship, refresh, correction and recovery receipts exist.
- Coverage gaps and unresolved resource/operator decisions remain transparent.
- Every in-scope package has acceptance or an explicit reviewed scope change.

**Required packages:** `PAPER-11.07`, `PAPER-14.07`, `PAPER-18.07`, `PAPER-19.07`, `PAPER-20.05`, `PAPER-20.06`, `PAPER-20.07`.

**Not established by this phase alone:** Permanent scientific completeness; Automatically authorized paid operations or outreach.

## Review and validation

Every work package has a distinct outcome, included/excluded scope, canonical future deliverables, specific tasks/subtasks, testable acceptance conditions, evidence requirements, owner role, prerequisites and source/context references. The referenced future deliverable paths need not exist during planning; they must be safe relative paths and unique per package.

Run the following offline checks from the repository root:

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_plan.py
python3 scripts/validate_research.py
python3 scripts/render_docs.py --check
python3 scripts/build_project_spec.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The planning validator checks schemas, unique IDs, hierarchy, task ownership, options, prerequisites, cycles, counts, coverage mappings, decision/release references, safe deliverable paths and provenance URL syntax. The renderer checks generated-document drift. These checks do not fetch sources, establish scientific truth, authenticate permissions, create GitHub resources or substitute for independent review.

A foundation phase remains unaccepted while required remote resources or readback are missing. Complete-program acceptance additionally requires every in-scope package to be accepted or changed through a recorded reviewed scope decision.
